WHY: per the SeatHolds contract (seat-holds.ts:5 'only commit() or release() ends one') releasing an already-committed hold is a double-end that can corrupt hold state, and the catch swallows the real failure — the old seat (booking.seatId) is never freed and stays leaked, while the caller gets an error implying the seat change did not happen. HOW: only release the hold if it has not been committed yet; e.g. track a committed flag or scope the try to just the update, and handle free separately.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: in changeSeat the try block calls holds.commit(hold) (line 26) then holds.free(booking.seatId) (line 27); the catch (line 29-31) unconditionally calls holds.release(hold). If free() throws, commit() has already ended the hold per the SeatHolds contract (seat-holds.ts:5 'only commit() or release() ends one'), so release() is a double-end, and the real failure (old seat not freed → leak) is swallowed while an error is thrown to the caller. No committed flag or scoped try exists. This is not a repeat of the earlier hold-leak entry (round-a-P29-hold-leak-on-create), which was about NOT releasing a hold after a failure; this finding is the opposite problem (releasing an already-committed hold), a distinct failure in the same operation.

delivered.text: When `holds.free(booking.seatId)` fails after `holds.commit(hold)` has already ended the hold, the catch's `holds.release(hold)` double-ends it and can corrupt hold state, while the old seat stays leaked and the caller gets an error implying the seat change did not happen. Only release the hold when it has not been committed, for example by tracking a `committed` flag and handling `free` separately.

WHY: 429 and every 5xx are dead-lettered instead of being requeued, so transient rate limits and server errors permanently drop deliveries, directly contradicting the comment on line 9. HOW: delete the `>= 400` drop branch; the final `return { kind: 'drop', reason: \`unexpected status ${status}\` }` already drops all other statuses, so 429 and 5xx reach their retry branches.
